relevance_note: Case report of one infant with LAD-1 and two ITGB2 variants: 'Genetic testing revealed ITGB2 c.850G>A (p.Gly284Ser) pathogenic variant and ITGB2 c.314T>C (p.Leu105Pro) likely pathogenic variant.'
method_note: Hand extraction, no table transcribed by script. One first-hand patient (single unnamed case-report patient, label 'patient'). Two previously published patients from reference (5) are in scope because the text gives a variant, sex, ancestry and a feature for each (labels 'ref (5) patient' = the homozygous c.314T>C patient, 'ref (5) patient 2' = the likely heterozygous patient with c.742-163_768del). Their ages '2- and 11-year-old' are not assigned to either patient, so age is not reported for both. 'Likely heterozygous' for ref (5) patient 2 is hedged, so zygosity is not reported. The gene for c.742-163_768del is printed only as 'partial deletion of exon 7', so gene_symbol_as_stated is 'not reported' for that row; variant type 'partial deletion of exon 7' not mapped to an enum. The HLA-identical sister (normal CD11b/CD18 expression, no genetic testing reported) is included as a relative, with no variant row. Sun et al. six compound heterozygotes and the c.850G>A carriers of refs (2, 3) are group-level only and get no rows. Contradiction: c.314T>C is called 'likely pathogenic' from genetic testing but later 'has an undefined pathogenicity'; the genetic-testing classification is recorded. Neutrophil count is reported both elevated (during illness) and within normal limits (at baseline, 4 mo 26 days); recorded as an observed neutrophilia row and a time-specific excluded row, checklist leukocytosis or neutrophilia observed. 'He did not have ... gastrointestinal disease' was taken to exclude the checklist items gastrointestinal infections and colitis or gastrointestinal inflammatory disease, but not diarrhea (a symptom). Age at diagnosis not recorded: the flow cytometry at 4 mo 19 days was 'consistent with LAD-1', but the age at genetic diagnosis is not stated. Age at onset not stated as such; first event in Table 1 at 1 mo 23 days recorded as feature onset only. Table 1 laboratory values not called abnormal in the text (e.g. IgE, eosinophil and lymphocyte subset counts) were not recorded as features. Variant type for the proband's variants is not stated (no 'missense' wording).
